parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price labels

indicators.note: only half of the word jogger is kept, its back half, so the front half is dropped

parts.note: the back half of jogger

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how enthusiastic every runner is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which suits the exclamation; here it just keeps the last three letters of jogger, GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen is enthusiastic and impatient to do something, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cares a lot about powered flight

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very concerned about flying in an aircraft with an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powered flight' suggests aviation; the flight is a flight of stairs, and a motor drives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is a set of steps (a flight) driven by a motor, so a witty cryptic-style definition.

clue.text: Hollywood actor assuming grandma's middle class

indicators.note: assuming in the sense of taking on or taking in, so the actor's name holds the other letter

parts.note: Richard Gere is a Hollywood film star

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word grandma

explanation.surface: A film star taking on the role of a grandmother's social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of artistic work, so it means class in that sense.

parts.note: a hiding is a heavy defeat, as is a rout
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that someone has gone into hiding in Spain, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' reads as concealment but means a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means ordinary or standard, the usual, which is what typical means.

clue.text: Insult is, for Macron, least significant

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
Emmanuel Macron is French president, and the French for is is est

explanation.surface: A French president's view that an insult is unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightest is the superlative of slight, meaning smallest in amount or importance.

indicators.note: in puts the fish inside the two letters for ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone hurls fish around on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling something is to throw it carelessly, so slings is a synonym for throws.

clue.text: Child at home with no money

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a cent is a small coin, a sum of money

explanation.surface: A child staying at home with no cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent is someone naive and guileless, like a young child, so the noun can stand for one.

clue.text: Hang around wife with little energy still

indicators.note: around tells us that hang's synonym goes round the other letters

parts.note: to hover is to hang in the air
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
E is the physics symbol for energy, a small version of the word

explanation.surface: A husband loiters near his wife, who still has little energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb of time attached to the scene, but it is the definition in the sense of 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and however both mean nevertheless, used to introduce a contrasting point.

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to give a statue's bust an all-over tan.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain people is to amuse or delight them, which is to please them.

clue.text: Runs inside bound to make you worn out

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation for runs within the word for bound

parts.note: bound means tied up
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Running while tied up is bound to exhaust you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'certain to', but bound is a synonym for tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired means exhausted, a direct synonym of worn out.

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters of 'of unions' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Confusion at the scheming of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Confusion is a state of puzzlement, the same as bewilderment.

clue.text: Server in restaurant leaving one something to drink

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter for one departs from the server's title

parts.note: a waiter serves at table in a restaurant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A waiter departing after giving a customer a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic drink, so it is an example of something to drink.

clue.text: Martial artist next to group staring suggestively

parts.note: Bruce Lee was a famous martial artist and film star
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A kung fu star beside a gang, ogling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a lascivious or knowing way, staring with suggestive intent.

parts.note: cove is old-fashioned British slang for a man or fellow
an embarrassed person goes red in the face

explanation.surface: An elderly man blushing when hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' suggests a father or husband; it is cove, a dated British word for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Embraced can mean included or took in, as a report covered every topic.

clue.text: The most suitable time to depart ancient city

indicators.note: to depart means to leave, so the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: the best means the most suitable

explanation.surface: Advice on the ideal moment to leave an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one T from THE BEST leaves the answer; it is the final T that departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and another of ancient Greece.

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: it, with the 's standing for 'is' as a link to the definition

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a fence if the price is good value.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of it's is short for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition, so only IT goes into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficient means working well without waste of money or effort, hence cost-effective.

parts.note: in means fashionable or current, of the now
a crease is a line, as on a face or a folded page

explanation.surface: An order to get into line at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line up' looks like one phrase meaning queue; 'up' alone is the definition, as a verb meaning raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To up a price is to raise it, so increase is a synonym of the verb up.

clue.text: Apparently these never forget the planes up in the air

indicators.note: up in the air means unsettled or in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aircraft in flight are said never to forget.
explanation.walkthrough: The planes in the air prompt thoughts of flying; it is just the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says these large animals have long memories, so 'apparently' they never forget.

clue.text: Beach view certain to be mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the words are said aloud and the result sounds like the answer

parts.note: to see something is to view it; sure means certain

explanation.surface: A seaside view that is sure to get talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The seashore is the land along the edge of the sea, so a beach is a stretch of it.

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the figure goes inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in water
a form is a figure or shape

explanation.surface: A shape cut into a lawn looks better.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reformed has changed for the better, as a reformed character is morally improved.

indicators.note: inside means the zero sits within the list word

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as is a roster
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chicken bread roll with no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken roll' suggests a sandwich, but the roll is a register of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel, so it is a kind of chicken.

clue.text: Drunkard — she regularly conceals bad smell

indicators.note: conceals means hides, so the selected letters wrap round the bad smell
regularly takes alternate letters, here the first and third of she

parts.note: pong is British slang for a stink

explanation.surface: A woman who drinks too much keeps hiding an unpleasant odour.
explanation.walkthrough: A pong is a British slang word for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponge is informal for a heavy drinker, one who soaks up alcohol.

parts.note: a port is a harbour

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the final letter of the synonym for too is dropped

parts.note: also means too, as well

explanation.surface: Entrances from the harbour are not quite tall enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Portals are grand doorways or entrances, so they are gateways.

clue.text: Snake European caught with tense face

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A snake-catcher from Europe meets a tense face-off.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one side or facet of something, as a building's face looks one way.

clue.text: Birds out of one's tree beginning to sing

parts.note: out of one's tree is slang for crazy, and so is cuckoo

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: first letter of sing

explanation.surface: Birds launching out of a tree to start their song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of one's tree' reads as leaving a tree; it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoos are a family of birds known for their two-note call.

parts.note: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Asks whether an American composer met his end behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Caged means locked up like an animal, so the question mark marks it as a loose sense of imprisoned.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to extend over an area
second meaning: British slang for a term in prison, also called porridge

explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is the oat breakfast, but in British slang it also means time spent in jail, and so does a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to extend over a surface and, informally, a prison sentence.

parts.note: a trip is a short holiday or outing

indicators.note: ending in means only the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: last letter of Scunthorpe

explanation.surface: A dreadful break that finishes in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Scunthorpe is an industrial town in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow's stomach lining and, figuratively, nonsense or worthless stuff.

indicators.note: heard means spoken aloud, so the word supposed's synonym sounds like the answer

parts.note: guessed means supposed or surmised

explanation.surface: Someone who comes to stay is expected to be audible.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person invited to stay or visit, so a visitor.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the synonym for alternative wraps round the period

parts.note: an option is an alternative or choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether there is another choice than going under the knife, and when.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure, so it is surgery done on a patient.

parts.note: to deter is to discourage, put off
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is discouraged by some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person who cleans; it is a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a chemical cleaning agent such as washing powder.

clue.text: Looks for small expressions of surprise

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
eek is an exclamation of alarm or surprise

explanation.surface: Someone searches for little gasps of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to search, so seeks is a synonym of looks for.
